description: A phosphate salt that lacks C-H bonds
docs.label: inorganic phosphate salt

description: A phosphate salt with C-H bonds
docs.label: organic phosphate salt

description: A pyrrolopyrimidine that is 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine substituted by a 1-[3-(cyanomethyl)-1-(ethanesulfonyl)azetidin-3-yl]-1H-pyrazol-4-yl group at position 5. It is an FDA approved selective Janus Kinase 1 and 2 (JAK1 and JAK2) inhibitor used for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.
docs.label: baricitinib

description: Salts and esters of phosphoric and oligophosphoric acids and their chalcogen analogues. In inorganic chemistry, the term is also used to describe anionic coordination entities with phosphorus as central atom.
docs.label: phosphate

description: A phosphate salt obtained by reacting 3,4-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole with one equivalent of phosphoric acid. It is a nitrification inhibitor and when used on crops, it prevents nitrogen loss from soil, increases nitrogen use efficiency, and boosts crop yields.
docs.label: 3,4-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole phosphate

description: A phosphate salt obtained by reaction leniolisib with one equivalent of phosphoric acid. It is used to treat activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase δ (PI3Kδ) syndrome in adults and children 12 years of age and older.
docs.label: leniolisib phosphate

description: Primaquine Phosphate is the phosphate salt form of primaquine, a synthetic, 8-aminoquinoline derivative with antimalarial properties. Although its mechanism of action is unclear, primaquine bind to and alter the properties of protozoal DNA. This agent eliminates tissue (exo-erythrocytic) malarial infection, preventing the development of the erythrocytic forms of the parasite which are responsible for relapses in Plasmodium vivax and ovale malaria. Primaquine is active against late hepatic stages (hypnozoites, schizonts).
docs.label: Primaquine Phosphate

description: A phosphate salt that is the diphosphate salt of histamine.
docs.label: histamine phosphate

description: A phosphate salt obtained by reaction ruxolitinib with one equivalent of phosphoric acid. Used for the treatment of patients with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis.
docs.label: ruxolitinib phosphate

description: A pyrazole substituted at position 1 by a 2-cyano-1-cyclopentylethyl group and at position 3 by a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4-yl group. Used as the phosphate salt for the treatment of patients with intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis, including primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis.
docs.label: ruxolitinib

description: A phosphate salt resulting from the reaction of equimolar amounts of tris and phosphoric acid.
docs.label: tris phosphate

description: A phosphate salt obtained by combining oritavancin with two molar equivalents of phosphoric acid. Used for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections caused or suspected to be caused by susceptible isolates of designated Gram-positive microorganisms.
docs.label: oritavancin bisphosphate

description: A member of the classo of biphenyls that is the amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-methyl-4'-(trifluoromethoxy)[1,1'-biphenyl]-3-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 6-(2,6-dimethylmorpholin-4-yl)pyridin-3-amine. Used (as its phosphate salt) for treatment of locally advanced basal cell carcinoma.
docs.label: sonidegib

description: A phosphate salt obtained by reaction sonidegib with two equivalent of phosphoric acid. Used for treatment of locally advanced basal cell carcinoma.
docs.label: sonidegib phosphate
